title: Sales enablement Positioning & messaging, competitive briefs, pitch deck, pricing guidance, case studies, security FAQ
author: Ava Ramirez
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook equips sales and solutions teams with concise positioning, competitor battlecards, a recommended pitch-deck outline, pricing guidance and negotiation levers, representative case studies, and a prospect-facing security FAQ. Use this document in discovery and pre-RFP engagement; sensitive sections (pricing models and negotiation guidance) are internal-only.

Audience: AEs, pre-sales/SEs, channel partners, and product-marketing.

Quick elevator pitch (30s)
- Redwood Inference provides a developer-first, production-grade inference platform that makes LLM-powered features predictable and economical across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- We combine a GPU-optimized serving runtime, smart routing, and observability so product teams can ship with consistent latency, lower unit cost, and enterprise controls.

Positioning pillars (primary messages)
1) Production-first performance and reliability
   - Predictable latency (SLO-backed tiers), throughput, and canary rollouts for safe launches.
   - Built-in fallback policies to reduce customer-facing downtime.
2) Unified deployment model
   - One API / same tooling across hosted, dedicated, and private (VPC/on-prem) modes.
   - Makes it easy to start hosted then move to dedicated/private as needs escalate.
3) Cost-aware controls and recommendations
   - Intelligent batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization profiles that reduce per-token cost without blind quality regressions.
   - Redwood Optimize provides actionable recommendations with expected cost delta.
4) Developer experience and integration speed
   - SDKs, quickstarts, curated prompt-sets and evals for validation.
   - Streaming, function/tool-calling and structured output support.

Persona-oriented messaging (two-line hooks)
- Product/Frontend engineers: "Ship high-quality LLM features quickly with predictable latency and low operational overhead."
- ML/Platform teams: "Standardize inference across teams with observability, rollout controls, and predictable unit economics."
- Security/Compliance: "Private deployment and KMS/HSM integrations for data residency and auditability."
- Engineering Leadership/Finance: "Reduce TCO with system-level batching, caching and model recommendations; commit to Reserved capacity for predictable cost."

Competitive brief / battlecard (summary)
Competitors covered: Major cloud AI platforms (AWS Bedrock, GCP Vertex AI), LLM API providers (OpenAI, Cohere), self-hosted inference vendors (Vendors X/Y), and GPU infra orchestration players.

Comparison matrix (summary)
| Dimension | Redwood | Cloud AI (Bedrock/Vertex) | OpenAI/Cohere | Self-hosted infra |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Deployment modes | Hosted / Dedicated / Private | Hosted / limited private | Hosted only | Self-hosted only |
| Performance controls | Kernel selection, continuous batching, KV caching | Managed but limited batching knobs | Limited perf tuning | Depends on customer engineering |
| Observability | Token-level cost/latency, route dashboards, regression alerts | Basic metrics / integrations | Usage metrics only | Varies widely |
| Enterprise controls | VPC, KMS/HSM, audit logs, SLA | VPC + cloud-native IAM | Limited enterprise features | Varies (no standard) |
| Pricing model | Usage + Reserved capacity / Enterprise license | Usage | Usage | Infra + ops cost |
| Time-to-value | Fast hosted onboarding + templates | Varied | Fast hosted | Long (engineering effort) |

How to win common competitor objections
- "We already use cloud vendor X": Emphasize predictable unit economics and inference-specific optimizations (batching, KV caching, quantization) that materially lower per-token cost and improve latency. Highlight migration playbooks and a trial with representative workload comparisons.
- "We run models in-house": Emphasize Redwood\u2019s value capture: less engineering time, standardized operations, built-in regressions/evals and SLO-backed availability. Offer a POC with side-by-side perf and cost measurement.
- "OpenAI's models are higher quality": Acknowledge model quality differences; focus on hosting flexibility (bring-your-own model), consistent latency/SLOs, and cost controls for scale. Offer evals on customer prompt-sets and quality/perf trade-off recommendations.

Pitch deck recommended outline (10\u201312 slides)
1. Cover + TL;DR value props (30s)
2. Problem: variability in latency, cost, and ops for LLMs
3. Solution: Redwood summary (unified runtime + orchestration)
4. How it works: serving runtime, compilation/kernel selection, smart routing, caching & batching
5. Deployment modes: Hosted / Dedicated / Private (incl. visuals of flow)
6. Observability & operations: dashboards, token-level cost, rollback/rollout controls
7. Cost and perf results: sample metrics from case studies (numbers below)
8. Security & compliance: KMS, VPC, SOC2, audit logging
9. Pricing options & commitment paths
10. Migration & onboarding plan (quickstart + SE checklist)
11. Case studies & references
12. Ask / next steps (POC, pricing, legal contact)

Demo / SE checklist (pre-demo prep)
- Gather: target model(s), typical prompt distribution (avg tokens/request, common long prompts), desired latency SLO, current monthly token volume, regulatory constraints (data residency), success metrics for the POC.
- Demo checklist: Live generation with streaming, show token-level latency/cost dashboards, simulate failure and show fallback, show model variant routing and canary rollout.
- POC success criteria: 1) meet latency SLO on 95th percentile, 2) reduce per-token cost by >= 20% (expected vs baseline), 3) integration in staging within 2 weeks.

Pricing guidance and negotiation levers
- Hosted API: pay-as-you-go usage pricing (per input/output token). Provide free trial credits and a representative cost-estimation worksheet during discovery.
- Dedicated (Reserved capacity): monthly/annual reserved GPU pools with committed throughput. Typical discounts 30\u201355% vs hosted on high-volume commitments; negotiation levers include committed spend, term length, and burst allowances.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): enterprise license (platform fee + support), professional services for deployment and hardening.
- Add-ons: extended observability retention, advanced evals and custom quantization profiles, premium SLAs.
- Example unit economics (illustrative):
   - Baseline: customer currently pays $0.012 per 1K tokens (hosted vendor).
   - Redwood hosted (after batching & caching): estimated $0.007 per 1K tokens (mix dependent).
   - Dedicated commit: equivalent $0.003-0.005 per 1K tokens depending on model mix and utilization.
Negotiation levers: committed volume, longer term (12/24 months), prepayment, trial scope (time-limited free credits), professional services package.

Procurement checklist for Enterprise deals
1) Legal: NDA, MSAs with data residency & breach notice timelines.
2) Security review: SOC2 Type II, penetration test reports, architecture whitepaper.
3) Compliance: data processing addendum (DPA), data retention & deletion options.
4) Network: VPC peering or private link options; required firewall/IP ranges.
5) KMS/HSM integration details and key rotation policies.
6) Support & SLAs: response times, incident escalation path, runbook access.

Representative case studies (anonymized customers)
- Case study A \u2014 Conversational commerce startup (AI-native)
  - Situation: High concurrency chat workload with 95th p99 latency spikes of 3.2s and monthly token cost $120k.
  - Redwood engagement: Hosted POC with prefix caching, batching and model quantization profile.
  - Outcome: 60% reduction in p95 latency (from 3.2s to 1.28s), 42% lower monthly token spend ($69.6k), time-to-production 3 weeks.
  - Why they chose Redwood: Developer speed + cost controls + simple upgrade path to Dedicated as volume grew.

- Case study B \u2014 Mid-market SaaS (document processing pipeline)
  - Situation: Heavy long-context embeddings + retrieval; infra ops team struggling with cost predictability.
  - Redwood engagement: Dedicated reserved capacity + caching and reranking optimization.
  - Outcome: 55% reduction in per-request compute cost, consistent throughput at 99.9% SLA, and predictable monthly billing enabling financial forecasting.

- Case study C \u2014 Regulated financial services (pilot)
  - Situation: Required private deployment and KMS integration for PII processing.
  - Redwood engagement: Private deployment with HSM-backed keys, audit logging, and on-prem option for an air-gapped test.
  - Outcome: Met compliance review within 8 weeks, successful internal audit, and enterprise contract signed.

Security FAQ for prospects (short-form, shareable)
Q: Where does customer data go when calling Redwood hosted API?
A: By default, hosted requests are processed in the customer-selected cloud region and are encrypted in transit and at rest. Logs, metrics, and payload retention follow the agreed retention policy; payloads can be disabled from being stored for customers that opt-out.

Q: Do you support VPC/private network connections for sensitive workloads?
A: Yes. We support VPC peering/private link for Dedicated and Private deployments; customers can choose private control plane options for additional isolation.

Q: How are encryption keys managed?
A: We integrate with customer KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and offer HSM-backed key stores for Private deployments. Customers may bring their own keys and maintain control over rotation.

Q: What compliance certifications do you hold?
A: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II. We provide penetration test summaries and support customer audits; specific regional certifications (e.g., ISO / industry-specific) are available via the compliance team on a case-by-case basis.

Q: How is model governance and data leakage addressed?
A: We provide model variant pinning, controlled model rollouts, and options to disable model training on customer data. For Private deployments, models and logs stay within the customer environment per deployment configuration.

Q: What observability and audit trails are available?
A: Token-level latency and cost breakdowns, per-route/model dashboards, request tracing hooks, and immutable audit logs with exportable retention windows are available.

Q: Can we run our own models on Redwood?
A: Yes \u2014 Redwood supports onboarding customer models where compatibility is met. We help with kernel selection, quantization guidance, and benchmarking.

Security & legal attachments to offer during RFP
- Architecture whitepaper (detailed network flows)
- SOC 2 Type II report (redacted)
- Pen test summary and remediation plan
- Data processing addendum (DPA) template

Sales play: Recommended POC structure (4 weeks)
Week 0: Discovery & kickoff \u2014 collect prompts, biz metrics, success criteria, legal kickoff.
Week 1: Baseline data collection and quick onboard (hosted sandbox) \u2014 run comparative evals.
Week 2: Performance optimization \u2014 apply batching, caching, quantization profiles, and run stress tests.
Week 3: Integration + observability demo \u2014 wire dashboards and tracing into customer staging.
Week 4: Wrap, executive review, pricing proposal, and next-steps (Dedicated/private offers if needed).

Collateral and templates included (links)
- One-page product cheat sheet (for AEs)
- ROI calculator (spreadsheet)
- POC checklist & success criteria template
- Draft MSA + DPA templates
- Pitch-deck template (Google Slides)

Ownership & maintenance
- Content owner: Go-to-market enablement (Ava Ramirez)
- Review cadence: Quarterly for messaging; immediate updates for pricing/competitor changes.
- Related teams: Product (for roadmap/feature calls), Eng (for perf numbers), Security/Compliance (for certs).

Appendix: Call scripts and discovery questions (short)
1) What model(s) are you currently using and how are they hosted?
2) What are your monthly token volumes and peak RPS?
3) What latency percentile matters most (p50/p95/p99) and what are your targets?
4) Are there regulatory or data residency constraints?
5) Which features are must-haves (streaming, tool calling, function outputs)?
6) Who owns procurement and security reviews?
